value.body: Food and beverage (F&B) service executives look after guests in hotel restaurants, bars, room service and banquets. They take orders, supervise service, coordinate with the kitchen and handle complaints. Employers include hotels, resorts, standalone restaurants, cruise lines and airline lounges.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BHM, a hospitality diploma, or a craft course

value.title: How you get in
value.body: BHM graduates usually join through campus placement into F&B as associates or through management trainee programmes that rotate through departments. Internship (industrial training) performance during the degree often decides placement offers.

value.title: At a glance
items: Long shifts, weekends and festival days are part of the job.
Common next steps: F&B supervisor, outlet manager, banquet manager.
Experience abroad (cruise lines, Gulf hotels) is a common route for some.
